title: Rubric bridging and score rescaling protocol for config/model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: As we roll model and config changes we observe score distribution shifts driven by rubric wording, cohort composition, and different LLM-judge behaviors. This ticket defines a repeatable protocol to produce cross-cohort, cross-rubric score mappings ("bridges") and a deterministic score-rescaling pipeline so that regression alerts and rollout decisions compare apples-to-apples.

Background: Multiple evaluation suites and rubrics have been developed over time (ad-hoc rubrics for new feature cohorts, specialized prompt-templates, and judge-model updates). Directly comparing raw numeric signals across these axes produces false positives and hides real regressions. We need a standardized way to: 1) map scores from a new rubric/config to the canonical baseline rubric; 2) quantify uncertainty in the mapping; and 3) integrate the mapping into the rollout and alerting pipeline.

Goals:
- Define a rubric-bridging methodology that supports: per-cohort anchors, LLM-as-judge synthesized pairwise comparisons, and human anchor calibration.
- Implement score-rescaling (calibration) using a combination of monotonic mapping (isotonic regression) and logistic scaling (Platt) with confidence bands.
- Add a model-change check in the evals pipeline that computes bridged metrics and flags meaningful deltas with uncertainty-aware thresholds.
- Provide a dashboard and runbook for engineering and SRE to interpret bridged metrics and execute rollbacks or partial rollouts.

Approach:
1) Anchor set: curate a compact, stratified human-labeled anchor set (~600 items) covering high/medium/low difficulty across cohorts. This set is the canonical reference; human labels define baseline score quantiles.
2) LLM-as-judge synthesis: use current judge-model versions to generate pairwise judgments and rankings on a larger synthesized dataset to increase sample coverage across score range. Use these pairs to learn monotonic mapping functions between rubric A (new) and rubric B (baseline).
3) Mapping model: fit isotonic regression to produce a monotonic mapping and a complementary Platt-scaling step to correct overall calibration. Fit a bootstrap to estimate confidence intervals on mapped scores. Persist mapping artifacts keyed by (model-version, eval-config, rubric-id).
4) Stability tests: run cross-validation across cohorts and perform out-of-sample checks to detect fragile mappings. If mapping uncertainty is high (CI width above threshold) mark metric as "unstable" and require manual review.
5) Integration: Add mapping computation as a post-eval step in the existing evals pipeline. Compute bridged metrics and expose both raw and bridged scores in the console and in metric-based rollouts. Add alert rules: e.g., bridged-metric drop >3% with p<0.05 triggers regression alert.
6) Human-in-the-loop: require human review for mappings that shift >5% of median bridged score or where customer-facing cohorts are affected.

Data and storage: store anchor set, synthesized judgments, and mapping artifacts in evals-storage S3 with metadata for traceability. Version mapping functions and record training seed, judge-model, and cohort filters.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full human re-labeling of every rubric is expensive; synthesis plus compact human anchors provides a pragmatic middle ground.
- Parametric fits (Platt) are simpler and lower-sample but can miss monotonic distortions; isotonic regression enforces monotonicity at cost of variance. We combine both to balance bias/variance.
- Per-cohort mappings increase accuracy but increase artifact count and maintenance; we will start with per-feature-cohort mappings and expand if needed.

Risks and mitigations:
- Judge-model drift changes mapping over time: mitigate by recording judge-model versions and recomputing mappings on judge updates or weekly for active rollouts.
- Small cohort sizes produce noisy bridges: flag as unstable and require manual review.

Outcomes and metrics:
- Successful mapping reduces false-positive regression alerts by >=50% in historical replay tests.
- Bridged metric correlates with human-A/B outcome at r>=0.75 on held-out tests.

Notes: detailed algorithms and experimental plan live in the Confluence doc (link below). Engineering will run initial experiments against the 2025-07 rollout cohort to validate methodology before wider adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical anchor set curated and human-labeled (>=600 items) with metadata and cohort tags
Prototype mapping algorithm implemented (isotonic + Platt) and reproducible via evals CI
Evals pipeline post-step computes bridged metrics and stores mapping artifacts with version ids
Console shows bridged and raw metrics side-by-side for at least 3 pilot cohorts
Alerting rules defined: bridged-metric drop >3% with significance triggers regression page
Runbook published with criteria for manual review and rollback steps
